requested.title: Relay claim callback accepts arbitrary GitHub installation IDs

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The relay branch accepts a valid HMAC state and positive numeric `installation_id`, then calls `bindRelayClaim` without checking that GitHub delivered the request or that the installation resulted from the state’s installation flow. The public `/api/relay/github/claim` endpoint will mint such a state for any active instance and any syntactically valid 64-hex-character code; it does not persist a pending claim or authenticate possession of the instance key. An attacker can self-register an active relay instance because `/api/relay/register` is intentionally open, request a claim URL/state for that instance, and directly invoke `/api/git/github/setup` with an unclaimed victim installation ID before the ten-minute expiry. `bindRelayClaim` confirms only that the GitHub App can resolve the supplied installation and that it is not already Cloud-connected or relay-claimed, then inserts the attacker-owned instance binding and creates the claim handoff row. The claim code is first stored only after this binding, so hashing it and calling it single-use does not establish that a claim was previously initiated. The normal callback-session mitigation is not reached by this branch, and the Next proxy explicitly excludes `/api/`, so no framework session protection applies. The resulting binding is security-significant: the attacker’s instance can submit arbitrary signed link-mirror entries and then satisfy the relay mint endpoint’s instance and repository checks to obtain scoped installation tokens; GitHub webhooks are also routed to that instance. Git history shows the ordinary setup callback was protected by session validation in `17f19b33`, while the vulnerable relay-specific bypass was introduced later in `bc097376`; it has not been subsequently fixed.
